content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (critical) — Article XII Indemnity.**

What I found:
- **Article XII (p0128–p0129)** is a one-way indemnity: Licensee indemnifies Licensor for its exercise of the licence, the conduct of its business, and any breach of any term. No Licensor indemnity exists anywhere in the agreement (only hit for "indemnif" in the document).
- **Article XIII (p0130)** compounds it: "UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCE SHALL LICENSOR BE LIABLE FOR ANY ACTIONS, CLAIMS OR THE LIKE ... THAT THE USE OF THE LICENSED TECHNOLOGY HAS RESULTED ... IN ANY INFRINGEMENT," and the warranty disclaimer strips non-infringement warranties.

This is walk-away territory under INDEMN (no Vendor IP indemnity plus a one-sided Customer indemnity), so it fails the fallback rather than sitting at it.

Redline validated (ok:true):
1. Added **Article XII(b)** — Licensor defends/indemnifies Licensee and affiliates for third-party IP infringement, breach of law, Licensor-caused data breaches, and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, with procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and expressly overriding Article XIII so the new indemnity is not neutralised by the liability exclusion.
2. Added **Article XII(c)** — reciprocal notice, control-of-defence, consent-to-settlement and cooperation mechanics.
3. Narrowed our indemnity to Licensee-provided content and Licensee's breach of applicable law, deleting the "solely responsible" opener and the business-conduct/any-breach limbs, with an express carve-out for third-party IP infringement claims.

The comment offers the fallback (customary modification/combination/specification exclusions and a 3× annual fees super-cap) as a landing zone.
